findings.title: CLASSIFIER fallback log mismatches actual mode
findings.problem: When a Switchyard entry declares mode=CLASSIFIER with no classifier_model configured, build_switchyard_routers logs that it will fall back to signal-only routing but never changes entry.mode/the resolved SwitchyardConfig.mode away from CLASSIFIER.
findings.impact: ProxySwitchyardRouter.pick_model() uses classifier_threshold (not signal_threshold) for this router, contradicting the logged claim and silently applying the wrong threshold.
findings.recommendation: Either construct the router with mode=RoutingMode.SIGNAL when falling back, or correct the log message to state the mode stays CLASSIFIER and clarify what the fallback actually does at request time.

findings.title: Switchyard router config redesigned self-configuring, diverging from spec
findings.problem: ModelSwitchyard is now a freely-authored list[ModelSwitchyard] entry (base_name/label hand-specified per entry) rather than the spec's single Optional[ModelSwitchyard] field with base_name/label auto-derived from a formula; commit history confirms this was a deliberate pivot ('Make Switchyard config a self-configuring list per capable model'). build_switchyard_routers treats a base_name collision as log.error + skip, not a load failure.
findings.impact: Reintroduces the manual per-router authoring the ticket's problem statement wanted removed as duplicated/error-prone; nothing enforces the old 1:1 base_name scheme for new entries; a typo'd base_name silently produces fewer routers than intended, discoverable only via logs.
findings.recommendation: Confirm with the spec/story owner whether this self-configuring shape is an approved design pivot (and update the spec to match) or whether formula-derived base_name/label plus load-time collision failure should be restored.

findings.title: RoutingDecision drops diagnostic fields with no migration note
findings.problem: RoutingDecision now carries only model/tier/classifier; confidence, signal_score, classifier_p_solve, crux, primary_rule, decision_source are gone, and the matching x-codemie-routing-signal-*/confidence/decision_source headers are dropped from SwitchyardMeta/SWITCHYARD_FIELD_TO_HEADER with no replacement.
findings.impact: The spec's non-goal was 'no change to the routing algorithm'; picking logic is preserved, but any downstream dashboard/log parser reading those headers now sees permanently missing fields with no error.
findings.recommendation: Confirm with the spec owner whether this field/header removal is an approved simplification (and document it for downstream consumers) or whether the fields need restoring.

findings.title: Agent-path routing badge never populates for LiteLLM auto-router
findings.problem: LiteLLMRouter never overrides candidate_models() (stays empty), so Router.build_chat_model() always returns the raw client for it, skipping RouterChatModel. Only RouterChatModel._agenerate calls stamp_routing_info(), and RoutingInfo.from_response() (used by AgentInvokeCallback/AgentStreamingCallback) now reads only that canonical stamp — the previous raw-header-reading extractor is gone.
findings.impact: The UI's routed-model/classifier-cost badge, fed by these two callbacks via LastRoutingTracker.observe(), never populates for a LiteLLM-autorouted response on the agent path.
findings.recommendation: Have the agent-path callbacks fall back to router.extract() (which does read raw headers) when the canonical stamp is empty, or otherwise ensure stamp_routing_info() runs for LiteLLMRouter-resolved models.

findings.title: Live-catalog models never carry litellm_router declaration
findings.problem: map_litellm_to_llm_model never sets litellm_router on the LLMModel it builds, so is_declared_litellm_router() is always False for any model sourced from the live LiteLLM/DIAL catalog, independent of whether LiteLLM's own proxy config.yaml declares that model_name as an auto-router.
findings.impact: Defeats router_factory._resolve_litellm_router (TokensCalculationCallback's classifier-usage/billed-model extraction silently loses tracking whenever the live catalog is preferred) and build_switchyard_routers' router-on-router guard for live-catalog capable/efficient models, with no error surfaced.
findings.recommendation: Propagate/derive litellm_router in map_litellm_to_llm_model from the live catalog's model_info (mirroring the static YAML shape), or explicitly document that live-catalog auto-router declarations are unsupported.

findings.title: Unrecognized libsy Step variant silently dropped
findings.problem: _consume_algorithm's match step: only handles Step.CallModel and Step.Done with no catch-all case; an unrecognized Step variant is silently skipped by the match (not even logged) and the async loop continues.
findings.impact: If a future Step variant is yielded (e.g. after the pinned nemo-switchyard commit is bumped), a call-shaped step could never get a response and run_stream could hang instead of failing fast. Reachability against the actual Step enum at the currently pinned commit could not be confirmed.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit case _: that logs and raises/breaks, matching the exhaustive-match pattern used elsewhere in this codebase.

findings.title: Router-on-router check defaults to wrong model when target missing
findings.problem: _resolve_switchyard_setup calls llm_service.get_model_details(target) for the switchyard config's capable/efficient model; when target is missing or misconfigured, get_model_details doesn't return None — it silently falls back to the catalog's default model, so details.is_declared_litellm_router() evaluates the default model's flag, not the missing target's.
findings.impact: A misconfigured/typo'd capable_model or efficient_model reference silently passes the router-on-router guard (evaluated against the wrong model) instead of being rejected as invalid.
findings.recommendation: Check llm_service.get_model_deployment_name(target) is None (or equivalent) first and reject the setup outright, rather than consulting get_model_details' default-model fallback.

findings.title: Router base_name silently resolves to default model
findings.problem: get_model_details() never returns None; when a name isn't found among real models/embeddings/routers it silently falls back to the catalog's default model, and get_llm_by_credentials (core/dependecies.py) calls it unconditionally with no rejection path for a router base_name reaching an execution path.
findings.impact: A router base_name (or any misconfigured model name) reaching this path is silently treated as the default model rather than raising, masking the real misconfiguration and violating the spec's required hard-fail behavior.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit check in get_llm_by_credentials/get_model_details that rejects (raises) when the resolved name is a router base_name.

findings.title: 4 unprefixed commits remain in branch history
findings.problem: git-workflow.md requires 'EPMCDME-####: Description' for repository commits; 4 commit subjects in 06d554d..HEAD ('Replace RPC channel with sentinel-file polling; add Agent Workspace precedent', 'Correct execution-container spec: gVisor is already the prod baseline', 'Explain why JOBS-mode over SHARED-mode in execution container spec', 'Add design spec: isolated execution container for code-driven workflows') carry no ticket prefix.
findings.impact: Documented commit-format standard is violated for part of the review range; squash-merge history retains unrelated, unprefixed commits even though their file changes were later removed.
findings.recommendation: Squash/rebase these 4 commits out of the branch history, or confirm the eventual squash-merge commit message itself carries the correct EPMCDME-14083 prefix.
